item.title: Stability of equilibria in discrete-time modified-gradient systems and the multivariate breeder's equation
item.description:
arXiv:2611.14756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The multivariate breeder's equation $\Delta ar z=G
abla\ln ar W$ is a widely used discrete-time modified-gradient system describing the evolution of continuous traits in organisms. This system could more conventionally be expressed as $x_{k+1}=x_k+P_k
abla f(x_k)$. For its continuous-time counterpart $x'=P(t)
abla f(x)$, it has been proven that an isolated local maximum of $f$ is uniformly stable whenever $P(t)$ is positive semidefinite, as is the case for the "$G$-matrix." Furthermore, the continuous time system is uniformly asymptotically stable when the maximum is an isolated critical point and $\int_0^\infty\lambda_1(P(t))\,dt=\infty$. We show that the literal discrete analog of this result is false: with constant positive definite $P$ the iterates can oscillate or diverge. The result is restored by a single additional hypothesis, a uniform bound on the largest eigenvalue of $P_k$, $\lambda_n$, such that $\lambda_n(P_k)\le 2/L$ where $L$ is a local Lipschitz constant of $
abla f$. Under this bound the maximum is uniformly stable; under a stricter version together with $\sum_k\lambda_1(P_k)=\infty$, the maximum is uniformly asymptotically stable. Given these hypotheses, a level-set estimate of the basin of attraction carries over. Both bounds are sharp, and each remaining hypothesis is shown to be necessary. Biologically, the bound says that genetic variance in every direction must be small relative to the curvature of log mean fitness; outside this regime the mean phenotype can overshoot a fitness peak as hypothesized by Fisher's geometric model. As further application of our results, the same conditions apply to the mean update of Gaussian evolutionary optimization algorithms, in which the covariance of the search population plays the role of $G$.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin J. Ridenhour

item.title: Sharpness of the acceleration-dependent H\"older exponent for the integrated density of states
item.description: arXiv:2611.15014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the acceleration-dependent H\"older exponent $1/(2\omega)$ for the integrated density of states is sharp in the supercritical regime. For every positive integer $k$ and every Diophantine frequency, we construct a real even trigonometric polynomial potential of degree $k$ such that, at a spectral edge, the Lyapunov exponent is positive, the acceleration is $k$, and the exact local H\"older exponent is $1/(2k)$. In particular, the $1/2$-H\"older regularity of the subcritical regime for Diophantine frequencies does not hold in general in the supercritical regime. The proof uses Aubry duality and a KAM iteration that adjusts the potential coefficients to make the dual cocycle reducible to a principal unipotent matrix. A comparison with an explicit reference family and symplectic block diagonalization then reduce the IDS estimate to a two-dimensional rotation-number estimate.
item.dc:creator: Jiabo Ye, Jiangong You

item.title: Canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction
item.description: arXiv:2611.15129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction. For any number of species and any rank of the fast subnetwork, the derivatives that enter the Krupa-Szmolyan conditions and coefficient are rational functions of the fluxes and the reciprocal concentrations. For a fast subnetwork of rank one, the dynamics is planar on stoichiometric classes and these forms are linear in the fluxes, extending our planar flux criterion; the criticality is an explicit cubic. When one species is fast, these forms decompose over the slow species, weighted by their reciprocal concentrations. The elementary-mode criterion then carries over, and the criticality depends on the composition of the slow pool, so one network can explode in either way. The obstruction that the slow flux cannot vanish on the fold is characterised by a Farkas certificate and a yield diagram decided on configurations of at most three reactions. Under four conditions on the critical curve, a canard point with $A\neq0$ unfolded by a rate constant gives the full canard explosion; with one fast species and a fast equation affine in the slow variable, these follow from sign conditions on the reactions and injectivity on the class. For fast subnetworks of higher rank, a centre-manifold reduction adds corrections through the group inverse of the fast Jacobian; in the Oregonator they make both canard points change criticality between its planar reduction and the full model. All results are proved; exact computations and simulations serve as independent checks.
item.dc:creator: Miruna-Mihaela Beldiman, Andrei-Dan Halanay

item.title: Rigidity of time changes of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flows on finite volume quotients
item.description: arXiv:2611.15182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the rigidity phenomenon of the time changed unipotent flows on general Lie groups. Under some spectral gap assumptions, we prove that every ergodic nonsplitting $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flow on a finite volume quotient space $\mathbf{G}/\Gamma$ is time changed rigid. We also prove that for $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flow, the splitting condition is equivalent to loosely Kroneckerness. Our result in particular applies to $\mathbf{G}=\mathbf{S}\ltimes\mathbf{N}$, where $\mathbf{S}$ is the identity component of a real semisimple linear algebraic group without compact factors and $\mathbf{N}$ is simply connected and connected nilpotent Lie group. These are extensions of [KVW21,LW25].
item.dc:creator: Huu-Hoan Nguyen, Daren Wei

item.title: Zero-Hopf Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.15221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur for dynamical systems that have a singularity where the linear part has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of purely imaginary eigenvalues. We call a zero-Hopf network a regular network whose adjacency matrix has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of complex eigenvalues with zero real part. In this work, we prove that there is an infinite number of zero-Hopf networks for which the zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur as a generic codimension-one phenomenon for the class of the network admissible smooth vector fields. Our results are achieved using the network adjacency matrices and the associated eigenvector structures. General results are presented for four-cell zero-Hopf networks concerning the network set of synchrony spaces. As a case study, we present a classification of all connected zero-Hopf 4-cell regular networks of valency two showing that, up to permutation of the cells, there are 9 distinct such networks. Moreover, the normal forms of these networks are computed using the method of Rink and Sanders (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 367 (2015) 3509--3548) for coupled cell networks. It is remarked that these normal forms are less simplified as the input symmetry of the network admissible smooth vector fields restricts the admissible normal form transformations. Nevertheless, the networks share a common coupling function normal form.
item.dc:creator: Manuela Aguiar, Ana Dias, Fahimeh Mokhtari

item.title: Stability of analytic monodromic singularities without curves of zero angular speed
item.description: arXiv:2611.15233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The aim of this work is to give conditions on the parameters of a family of analytic planar vector fields with a fixed Newton diagram and a monodromic singularity in order to guarantee that the coefficient (generalized first Lyapunov constant) of the linear part of the Poincar\'e map has an explicit formula. We revisit using this formalism some monodromic examples appearing in the literature and also we apply the results to other families were, as far as we know, the stability problem was open.
item.dc:creator: Isaac A. Garc\'ia, Jaume Gin\'e

item.title: Universal Realization of Milnor Attractors in Low Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.15353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the realization problem for Milnor attractors on compact metric spaces and establish a general sufficient criterion for universal realization. In particular, we prove that every smooth compact one-dimensional manifold, with or without boundary, and every smooth closed two-dimensional manifold has the property that each nonempty closed subset is the Milnor global attractor of a continuous self-map. If the manifold is connected, the realizing map may be chosen to be a homeomorphism. We also investigate the realization problem on selected one-dimensional continua and exhibit spaces for which universal realization fails.
item.dc:creator: Jana Hant\'akov\'a, Michaela Ml\'ichov\'a

item.title: On the structure of the sets of connections between libration points and some applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.15361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a methodology for the global description of the sets of heteroclinic and homoclinic connections between the center manifolds of the collinear libration points of the spatial circular Restricted Three-Body Problem. The approach builds on high-order parameterizations of the center-stable and center-unstable invariant manifolds and uses them to extract global information on how connections are organized across broad energy ranges. It involves: (a) constructing connectivity maps at the level of invariant tori, which encode which tori in the neighborhoods of $L_1$ and $L_2$ are connected through heteroclinic and homoclinic trajectories; (b) refining this description to the level of individual connections by computing traces of torus--center manifold connections and using them to determine the number and distribution of distinct connecting trajectories between selected pairs of tori. Results are given for the Earth--Moon and Sun--Earth problems, together with examples illustrating how the resulting connectivity information can be used to design heteroclinic and homoclinic pseudo-trajectories with different purposes.
item.dc:creator: Miquel Barcelona, \`Alex Haro, Josep-Maria Mondelo

item.title: Geometric structure of Green currents for holomorphic correspondences on projective surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.15554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f$ be a holomorphic correspondence on a complex projective surface $X$ such that $f^{-1}$ is also holomorphic. Assume that the action of $f^*$ on cohomology is simple and that the dynamical degrees of $f$ satisfy $d_1>\max\{d_0,d_2\}$. We prove that the Green currents $T^\pm$ associated with $f$ are woven. We also provide a large family of examples of holomorphic correspondences satisfying our assumptions, obtained as generic complete intersections in $X\times X$.
item.dc:creator: Muhan Luo, Marco Vergamini

item.title: Equidistribution of Hecke neighbours and continued fraction patterns
item.description: arXiv:2611.15558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove uniform tightness of Hecke neighbours of any probability measure of positive entropy that is invariant and ergodic under the diagonal flow. As an application, we confirm a conjecture of Einsiedler concerning a homogeneous dynamics analogue of an equidistribution theorem of Johnson and Rudolph on the torus. We also obtain applications to continued-fraction patterns in arithmetic sequences and to the \(p\)-adic Littlewood conjecture. Our proof studies escape of mass using dynamics on the boundary of the Chabauty compactification of the space of lattices, together with averaging operators defined by leafwise measures along horospherical subgroups.
item.dc:creator: Menny Aka, Segev Gonen Cohen

item.title: Autonomous Neural Adaptive Control as a Self-Consistent Transfer Operator
item.description: arXiv:2611.15649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study autonomous neural adaptive control, where the controller modifies the physical dynamics while the data generated by the physical dynamics itself drive subsequent parameter updates. We formulate the coupled evolution of the physical state distribution and controller parameters through a self-consistent transfer operator. Assuming that the physical dynamics under each fixed controller admits a unique invariant distribution, we characterize adaptive equilibria through a finite-dimensional self-consistency equation for the stationary mean learning update. We establish existence using Brouwer degree, without requiring global convexity, and reduce uniqueness to uniqueness of the corresponding zero. Under suitable differentiability and spectral-gap assumptions, we derive a finite-dimensional criterion for local exponential convergence of both the physical distribution and controller parameters at sufficiently small positive learning rates. The criterion involves the Jacobian of the reduced equation, computed using linear response to include the effect of controller-induced changes in the invariant distribution. The asymptotic slow relaxation time scales inversely with the learning rate. We rigorously verify the assumptions and apply the theory to a noisy Duffing-type system with a neural residual compensator, providing a nontrivial example of adaptive control with provable existence, uniqueness, and local stability of an adaptive equilibrium. Numerical experiments illustrate statistical feedback and the role of time-scale separation.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Galatolo, Vittorio Lippi

item.title: Density of periodic measures on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)\backslash\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$ with prescribed arithmetic information
item.description: arXiv:2611.15685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be the diagonal flow on the modular space $X_2$, and let $\mathcal{S}_f$ be the set of positive square-free numbers, which is identified with the set of all real quadratic fields via the natural map $d\mapsto \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt d)$. In this paper, we prove that, for any finite subset $A\subseteq\mathcal{S}_f$, there exists a density-zero set $B\subseteq\mathcal{S}_f\setminus A$ such that the set of all $F$-periodic measures with associated quadratic fields from $B$ is dense in the set of all $F$-invariant measures on $X_2$.
item.dc:creator: Lifan Guan, Chengyang Wu, Weisheng Wu

item.title: Almost sure behaviour of empirical measures for intermittent maps whose return time distribution is 1-regularly varying
item.description: arXiv:2611.15955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article we study sets of limit points $\mathcal{L}$ for the sequence of empirical measures of intermittent maps with several equally sticky neutral fixed points. Such intermittent maps come with a parameter $\alpha > 0$ which determines the "stickiness" of the neutral fixed points. When $\alpha \neq 1$, it is known that two different behaviours can occur: either $\mathcal{L}$ is almost surely the singleton $\{\mu\}$ where $\mu$ is an absolutely continuous invariant probability measure; or $\mathcal{L}$ is almost surely given by the entire simplex $\pi\mathcal{S}$ of invariant measures supported at the neutral fixed points. We study the case that $\alpha = 1$ and show that neither of these two behaviours occur and that $\mathcal{L}$ is almost surely equal to a star-shaped subset of the simplex $\pi \mathcal{S}$. Moreover, we show that when slowly varying functions are introduced one can obtain a large range of different behaviours, including both the possible outcomes when $\alpha \neq 1$. Our results apply to a large class of intermittent interval maps as well as parabolic rational maps of the Riemann sphere.
item.dc:creator: Douglas Coates, Tanja I. Schindler

item.title: The Levitt--Yoccoz gasket: dynamics, Hausdorff dimension and norm exponent
item.description: arXiv:2611.15996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In S.P.~Novikov's problem on plane sections of 3ply periodic surfaces, the author and I.\,A.~Dynnikov showed that, for the $\mu$-cube, the directions lying in no stability zone form the union of a fractal set $N$, the Levitt--Yoccoz gasket (projectively equivalent to the Rauzy gasket), and of its images under the sign changes of the coordinates. $N$ is the limit set of a parabolic projective iterated function system $P\Gamma_N$ generated by a semigroup $\Gamma_N\subset SL_3(\mathbb Z)$, and each zone is labelled by a primitive integer vector, its soul. We show that $N$ is the global attractor of $P\Gamma_N$ and that the chain graphs of $P\Gamma_N$ and its Hutchinson map consist of a single node. Building on the theorem of Jiao--Li--Pan--Xu and Jurga that $\dim_H N$ equals the affinity exponent of $\Gamma_N$, we prove $1.6853<\dim_HN=\dim_BN<1.6854$. For some class of cut-out gaskets $K$, we bound $\overline{\dim}_B K$ from both sides by the norm exponent $s_N(\Gamma)$. The norm exponent $s_N$ of $G_N$, the counting exponent of the souls, is Baragar's exponent of the Markoff--Hurwitz equation $x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2+x_4^2=ax_1x_2x_3x_4$. We prove $2.4411\le s_N\le2.4465$, improving Baragar's bounds, and $\frac23 s_N\le\dim_H N\le\frac12(1+s_N)$, which proves a conjecture by Gamburd, Magee and Ronan; and we show that the exponent of the equation in six variables exceeds $3$, answering a question of Baragar. For the three-dimensional Levitt--Yoccoz gasket $G\subset\mathbb RP^3$ we prove $2.74\le s_N(\Gamma_G)\le2.777$ and $\dim_H G\le2.3885$. Finally, for the renormalization flow of Avila, Hubert and Skripchenko, we show that the invariant measure they introduce is the Gibbs measure at the parameter $s_N$ and that $s_N$ is the maximal entropy per unit time of the return map, attained only by this measure. So, the diffusion exponent of their chaotic plane sections is less than 0.7766.
item.dc:creator: Roberto De Leo

item.title: Invariant random compacts for $\times p, \times q$ on the circle
item.description: arXiv:2611.16008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for multiplicatively independent natural numbers $p,q \ge 2$, if $\mu$ is a Borel probability measure on the space $\mathcal{K}(\mathbb{T})$ of nonempty compact subsets of the circle $\mathbb{T}$ which is invariant under the induced actions of both multiplication by $p$ and $q$, and $\mu$-a.e. $Y$ has positive Hausdorff dimension, then $\mu$-a.e. $Y$ is equal to $\mathbb{T}$.
item.dc:creator: Scott Schmieding

item.title: Nondifferentiability on Irrational Invariant Graphs of Smooth Area-Preserving Twist Maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.16294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a fixed irrational rotation number and every $1\le r<\infty$, we construct an exact area-preserving $C^r$ twist map preserving a Lipschitz graph. The set of nondifferentiability points has Hausdorff dimension $d=2/(r+1)$ and zero $d$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. At the same rotation number, we construct a $C^\infty$ twist map whose invariant graph is nondifferentiable on exactly one two-sided orbit. The dynamics on these graphs has wandering intervals.
item.dc:creator: Lin Wang

item.title: Visibility graphs of irregularly sampled two-dimensional fields via Voronoi tessellations
item.description: arXiv:2611.16336v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visibility graphs map a time series into a network by linking two data whenever the straight line between them is not obstructed by intermediate data. Their extension to two-dimensional fields has so far been restricted to regular lattices, where visibility is checked along a finite number of lattice directions. We propose a definition for scalar data sampled at arbitrary, irregularly scattered points of the plane. Each point is assigned its Voronoi cell, so that the data become a landscape of prisms, and two points are linked when the line of sight between them clears the cells crossed by the connecting segment. This yields horizontal ($\HVGV$) and natural ($\NVGV$) Voronoi visibility graphs that reduce exactly to the classical horizontal and natural visibility graphs when the points are collinear, contain the Gabriel graph of the point set, and can be built by an exact walk through the Delaunay triangulation. For uncorrelated heights, the horizontal graph depends only on the ranks of the data, so its statistics are independent of the marginal distribution. The probability that two points see each other is $2/[(M+1)(M+2)]$, where $M$ is the number of Voronoi cells crossed, which reduces the problem to the geometry of the tessellation. For Poisson points this gives a degree distribution with a scale-free tail $P(k)\simeq(\pi^3/4)\,k^{-2}$ and a mean degree that grows as $(\pi^3/8)\ln N$, in contrast with the finite value $\langle k\rangle=4$ of one-dimensional series. Two dimensions are therefore the marginal case in which isotropic horizontal visibility ceases to be local. Numerical simulations with up to $N=1.28\times10^5$ points support these predictions.
item.dc:creator: Francisco J. Mu\~noz, Juan Carlos Nu\~no

item.title: Weighted summability criteria for stability and instability of discrete dynamics with general growth rates
item.description: arXiv:2611.16352v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Following the time rescaling introduced by Dragi\v{c}evi\'{c} and Silva in their paper [Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst. Ser. S 18 (2025), 3917--3944], we establish several criteria for uniform $h$-stability and uniform $h$-instability of discrete evolution cocycles. In particular, these asymptotic properties are characterized by suitable weighted summability conditions under uniform $h$-boundedness and uniform $h$-decay assumptions, respectively. Explicit examples show that the respective assumptions cannot be omitted. Our results cover a wide range of discrete growth rates $h$, including exponential and polynomial ones. Furthermore, working in the general setting of discrete evolution cocycles, we provide a framework for discrete evolution families and discrete cocycles.
item.dc:creator: Ariana G\u{a}in\u{a}, Cristian L\u{a}zureanu, Nicolae Lupa

item.title: Quantitative flocking of Cucker-Smale flocks under time-delay and noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.16613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the asymptotic flocking dynamics of the delayed stochastic Cucker-Smale (in short, DSCS) model driven by agent-wise independent, component-wise multiplicative Brownian noise. The simultaneous interplay of stochastic perturbations and time delay yields fundamental challenges to asymptotic stochastic flocking analysis, as the communication weight may lose a uniform positive lower bound, while the velocity moment is no longer monotone. To overcome these difficulties, we present a sufficient framework and an analytical tool combining the method of time-varying effective region and Lyapunov functional approach with time-delay corrections. This approach avoids any reliance on uniformly positive communication weights or monotone velocity moments. The proposed approach recovers sufficiently strong effective velocity alignment despite stochastic fluctuations and delay effects. As a consequence, we establish the mean-square stochastic flocking with an explicit polynomial convergence rate. The admissible decay exponent is determined by the communication kernel exponent and the orders of the spatial and velocity history moments. These results establish a quantitative theory for long-time stochastic flocking under simultaneous delay and multiplicative noise, and we provide a positive answer to an open problem raised by~[R. Erban, J. Haskovec, Y. Sun, SIAM J. Appl. Math., 76, 1535--1557 (2016)]. We also develop robust analytical tools applicable to delayed stochastic collective dynamics with degenerate communications.
item.dc:creator: Seung-Yeal Ha, Xinyu Wang, Chen Wu, Fanqin Zeng

item.title: Quantitative Accumulation of Invariant Circles Near a Non-splitting Separatrix
item.description: arXiv:2611.16616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a smooth area-preserving cylinder map with a non-splitting separatrix and an exact symplectic linearization at its saddle, we prove accumulation by smooth essential invariant circles when the boundary transition is sufficiently $C^4$-close to a translation. As an application, we give an answer to Herman's open problem in 1983.
item.dc:creator: Deyu Kong, Lin Wang

item.title: Infectious Disease Horizon in Emerging Infectious Diseases
item.description: arXiv:2611.16675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Emerging infectious diseases often spread freely before an outbreak is detected, yet the duration of this free-transmission period and the infection size accumulated during this period are difficult to quantify. These quantities directly affect forecasts of subsequent transmission dynamics, estimates of infection size, and decisions regarding prevention and control measures. In this study, we propose and compute the infectious disease horizon (IDH)-the time span from when an infectious disease begins spreading to when it is first detected-and examine its antecedents and consequences. First, based on the SEAIR free-transmission model, we derive transmission characteristics, including the generation interval, the serial interval, the basic reproduction number, and the effective reproduction number, and describe the incidence using a renewal equation. Second, by considering two detection routes, we further obtain the distribution and mean of the IDH under different detection settings and quantify the infection size at the time of outbreak detection. Third, intervention measures are incorporated to derive a post-detection transmission model with generally distributed stage durations, followed by the derivation of the corresponding model under exponentially distributed stage durations and the determination of the final infection size. Finally, under the exponential-distribution assumption, the model is applied to the COVID-19 outbreak in Xi'an. The unified framework developed in this study provides a theoretical basis for evaluating early surveillance capacity for emerging infectious diseases, optimizing testing strategies, and determining the intensity of prevention and control measures after outbreak detection.
item.dc:creator: Miaomiao Lv, Juan Zhang, Zhen Jin

item.title: Data-Driven Discovery and Rigorous Certification of Periodic Solutions in Infinite-Dimensional Dynamical Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.16706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we consider a standard regression technique for time series analysis which fits a low-dimensional proxy system to a higher (even infinite) dimensional target model. We then propose a novel diagnostic that exploits a-posteriori computer-assisted proofs, and try to certify the existence of a true periodic solution of the target, nearby. When successful, this certification procedure provides mathematically rigorous information about how well an invariant structure in the proxy approximates a corresponding invariant structure in the target model. To illustrate the utility of the procedure, we develop surrogates using time series data from the Mackey--Glass delay differential equation, and for the Kuramoto--Sivashinsky (KS) partial differential equation, using periodic boundary conditions for forecasting and Neumann boundary conditions for certification. In both test cases we extract invariant dynamics from low-dimensional proxies and use this to validate the existence of corresponding structures in the targets.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Loh, J. D. Mireles James

item.title: ControlHarbor: A Benchmark for Control Design by Coding Agents
item.description: arXiv:2611.16867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents, i.e., language models run by a harness, can now write, run and debug software autonomously. This raises the question of whether they can also carry out control system design. In this paper, we consider control system design as a task for LLM agents and grade the designed controller as control engineers do: the controller is given in a single Python file mapping measurements to actions, evaluated on held-out seeds against an ordered set of requirements, under specified physical perturbations and structural certificates, without using neural networks. We formulate the task as a chance-constrained feasibility problem and instantiate it in ControlHarbor, a benchmark of 44 tasks over 13 plants, which includes network consensus, vehicle platooning, the MuJoCo hopper, walker and humanoid. The tasks are packaged in the Harbor format, so that any agent harness can be run against them, and the same environments also serve learning algorithms other than LLMs, such as reinforcement learning (RL), under the same evaluation. With ControlHarbor, we observe that the controllers designed by three frontier coding agents, Claude Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Sonnet 5.5, reach the RL return on every parity task, but only in a minority of sessions. We also observe that the controllers certified for return alone usually fail under perturbations. When robustness is part of the specification, a structured design meets it at the RL return on the humanoid task, where domain-randomised RL does not; under large pushes, domain-randomised RL succeeds and no designed controller does. The benchmark, the controllers, and their grades are released.
item.dc:creator: Jieqiang Wei, Fahad Ali, Jonny Reichwald, Silun Zhang

item.title: Dimension drop for superlevel sets of the uniform Littlewood constant
item.description: arXiv:2611.17189v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and $Q\ge 1$, set $F_Q(x,y)=Q\min_{1\le q\le Q}\lVert qx\rVert\lVert qy\rVert$, where $q$ ranges over positive integers and $\lVert\cdot\rVert$ denotes distance to the nearest integer. The set on which the uniform Littlewood constant $L=\limsup_{Q\to\infty}F_Q$ is positive has full Hausdorff dimension. We prove that for every fixed $c>0$ the superlevel set $\{L\ge c\}$ has Hausdorff dimension strictly less than two. More precisely, the Lebesgue measure of $\{(x,y)\in[0,1]^2:F_Q(x,y)\ge c\}$ is $O_c(Q^{-\kappa(c)})$ for some $\kappa(c)>0$ and all $Q\ge 2$. The proof combines large deviations for one diagonal action on the space of unimodular lattices with effective equidistribution of expanding horospheres for another.
item.dc:creator: Shahriar Mirzadeh

item.title: Structure-Preserving Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Dynamics on Arbitrary Time Scales
item.description: arXiv:2611.17219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron combines a passive membrane law with threshold-triggered firing and reset. We formulate this hybrid neuron model, under constant input, on an arbitrary Hilger time scale $\mathbb{T}$. Our central result is that, after the first spike, the firing times satisfy $t_{n+1}=\Pi_{\mathbb{T}}^{+}(t_n+T_c)$, where $T_c$ is the classical reset-to-threshold travel time. This recursion requires no periodicity, homogeneity, or translation invariance of $\mathbb{T}$; it holds for every time scale that is unbounded above. To preserve the passive membrane physics, we use the inverse cylinder transformation to construct a positively regressive coefficient $p_m$. The resulting delta-dynamic equation is exactly the restriction to $\mathbb{T}$ of the classical continuous-time LIF trajectory. By contrast, the direct transcription $V^\Delta=-(V-V_\infty)/\tau_m$ exhibits graininess-dependent sign reversal and amplification at coarse right-scattered points. The first firing time is the forward projection of the classical continuous threshold-crossing time onto $\mathbb{T}$, and, when the graininess is bounded by $\mu^\ast$, the per-event forward-projection delay -- from each reset to the next realized firing time, relative to the continuous crossing time computed from that same reset -- is bounded above by $\mu^\ast$. On $\mathbb{T}=h\mathbb{Z}$ we obtain the explicit lattice-quantized law $T_{\mathrm{ISI}}^{(h)}=h\lceil T_c/h\rceil$, which converges to the classical continuous-time inter-spike interval as $h\to0^+$. The framework therefore separates preserved membrane physics from the temporal opportunity structure imposed by the time domain. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic Hilger-calculus treatment of a threshold-and-reset LIF spiking neuron on an arbitrary time scale.
item.dc:creator: Billur Kaymak\c{c}alan (University of Turkish Aeronautical Association), Behiye \.{I}layda Sel\c{c}uk (Bilkent University)

item.title: Luenberger observers for two-gene regulatory networks with sigmoidal regulation: explicit observability conditioning, polytopic convergence certificates, and a logistic--Hill comparison
item.description: arXiv:2611.17232v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Only a few species of a gene regulatory network can be measured, so the others must be reconstructed by a state observer, and how well this works depends on the function chosen to describe regulation. We examine this for the two-gene negative feedback loop with one measured protein, for monotone regulation functions including the logistic function and the Hill function with its leaky and shifted variants. Using standard tools, we show that the answer is set by the smallest and the largest slope of the regulation function on the concentrations visited. For every function considered, the unmeasured concentration can be recovered from the measured signal and its rate of change, with an error sensitivity set by the smallest slope. A Luenberger observer with explicit gains converges exponentially from any initial guess and tolerates bounded measurement noise whenever a checkable matrix condition involving only the largest slope holds, as it does for every model examined with bounded slopes. The guaranteed rate cannot exceed the degradation rate of the unmeasured protein unless the smallest slope is positive, and faster rates then hold only for small initial errors. All reported rates are certified from above and below. At matched threshold and steepness, no family is uniformly better: the logistic function is better conditioned when the threshold lies mid-range, leaky or shifted Hill functions when it lies low. Hill functions with exponent below one have an unbounded slope at zero concentration and lose the global guarantee, which logistic and shifted Hill functions keep.
item.dc:creator: Ismail Belgacem

item.title: On $L^p$ density of self-similar measures and Bernoulli convolutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.17277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that an absolutely continuous self-similar measure has an $L^p$ density for some $p>1$. Moreover, explicit examples of Bernoulli convolutions with a continuous density are established.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Kittle, Constantin Kogler

item.title: Countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit
item.description: arXiv:2611.17315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit. Given an infinite compact metric countable space $X$, we show that $\mathcal{DO}(X)$, the collection of continuous functions on $X$ to itself admitting a dense orbit, is always nonempty. We then classify the systems in $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ up to topological conjugacy in terms of the second Cantor--Bendixson derivative $X^{(2)}$: if $X^{(2)} = \emptyset$ then all systems in $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ are mutually conjugate, while if $X^{(2)} \neq \emptyset$ then $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ contains $2^{\aleph_0}$ pairwise nonconjugate systems. The proof of the latter relies on a gluing construction for countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit, which is of independent interest. We also show that $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ is nowhere dense in $C(X,X)$ with the compact-open topology. We also study the Ellis semigroup $E(X,f)$ of a countable dynamical system. We characterize, under the assumption that $|\omega(x,f)| = 1$ for each $x \in X^{(1)}$, when the nontrivial functions of $E(X,f)$ are continuous. In particular, for the family constructed on spaces with $|X^{(2)}| \geq 2$, every nontrivial function of the Ellis semigroup is discontinuous.
item.dc:creator: Jhon P\'erez-Remolina, Carlos Uzc\'ategui-Aylwin

item.title: A hyperbolic area proof of the Kahn-Lyubich Covering Lemma and its generalization
item.description: arXiv:2611.17326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Covering Lemma of J. Kahn and M. Lyubich is a fundamental analytic tool for controlling conformal moduli of annuli under branched coverings of finite degree. In the last several decades, it has played a crucial role in establishing rigidity of multicritical polynomial and rational maps. The classical proof uses the Near-Degenerate Regime as the main mechanism. In this short note, we prove this lemma using hyperbolic area and the Dirichlet energy. We also establish a version of the Covering Lemma for holomorphic maps of infinite degree. Our argument is inspired by recent applications of the hyperbolic area method to the study of wandering domains in rational and transcendental dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Kostiantyn Drach

item.title: The N-Body Problem on Coadjoint Orbits
item.description: arXiv:2504.01272v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show (Theorem 3) that the symplectic reduction of the spatial $n$-body problem at non-zero angular momentum is a singular symplectic space consisting of two symplectic strata, one for spatial motions and the other for planar motions. Each stratum is realized as coadjoint orbit in the dual of the Lie algebra of the linear symplectic group $Sp(2n-2)$. The planar stratum arises as the frontier upon taking the closure of the spatial stratum. We reduce by going to center-of-mass coordinates to reduce by translations and boosts and then performing symplectic reduction with respect to the orthogonal group $O(3)$. The theorem is a special case of a general theorem (Theorem 2) which holds for the $n$-body problem in any dimension $d$. This theorem follows largely from a ``Poisson reduction'' theorem, Theorem 1. We achieve our reduction theorems by combining the Howe dual pair perspective of reduction espoused by Lerman-Montgomery-Sjamaar with a normal form arising from a symplectic singular value decomposition due to Xu. We begin the paper by showing how Poisson reduction by the Galilean group rewrites Newton's equations for the $n$-body problem as a Lax pair. In section 6.4 we show that this Lax pair representation of the $n$-body equations is equivalent to the Albouy-Chenciner representation in terms of symmetric matrices.
item.dc:creator: Holger Dullin, Richard Montgomery

item.title: Chaotic-Periodic Alternation in a Financial System with Double Delays
item.description: arXiv:2611.14702v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we present the chaotic-periodic alternation phenomenon within a three-dimensional nonlinear financial system subjected to Pyragas-type time-delayed feedback, as well as the lag effect of the interest rate in the price index dynamics. Through numerical analysis, transitions to chaos, including period-doubling cascades, period-halving routes, and incommensurable-period dynamics are characterized. The emergence of chaotic-periodic alternation are found and described. Results suggest that minor timing misalignments in the inner dynamics of a financial system, as well as those considered in the feedback loop can induce systemic volatility.
item.dc:creator: Jes\'us Salinas-Gutierrez, V\'ictor F. Bre\~na-Medina, Marcos \'Angel Gonz\'alez-Olvera, Anah\'i Flores-P\'erez

item.title: On the statistical reliability of chaotic simulations at reduced precision
item.description: arXiv:2611.15344v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reduced-precision arithmetic is increasingly used to accelerate scientific simulation, while AI workloads are driving its growing prominence in hardware design. Yet small arithmetic errors do not necessarily imply accurate statistics. Finite representation limits spatial resolution, while rounding can merge trajectories that should separate in chaotic systems, progressively concentrating probability on a shrinking collection of computer states. This redistribution can distort statistical averages well before periodicity becomes apparent; furthermore, disjoint computational basins can induce an initialisation bias, even when the intended equilibrium statistics are independent of the initial ensemble. We use functional graphs and their transfer operators to connect these pathologies to bounds on statistical bias, the duration of accurate averaging, and the effect of reducing precision. Exhaustive numerical experiments on four chaotic maps, with 1-24 significand bits and the 24-bit endpoint matching IEEE FP32, show how initially accurate ensembles drift towards incorrect statistics, with lower precision often bringing this deterioration forward. Stochastic rounding substantially extends some useful averaging windows but leaves others severely biased. Longer computed trajectories can therefore worsen inferred statistics, and a finite average can outperform the "infinite-time" computer average by orders of magnitude. This exposes a risk of statistically biased inference at reduced precision and provides a further motivation for collecting statistics from ensembles of shorter trajectories.
item.dc:creator: Ross Ah-Weng, Peter V. Coveney

item.title: Shift-Symmetric Configurations in $d$-Dimensional Cellular Automata: Enumeration, Bounds, Irreversibility, and Detection
item.description: arXiv:2611.15751v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A configuration of a cellular automaton on the $d$-dimensional torus $\mathbb{Z}_n^d$ is shift-symmetric if it is fixed by some nonzero translation. Banda, Caughman, Cenek, and Teuscher (Chaos 29, 063120, 2019) enumerated these configurations in two dimensions and drew dynamical and algorithmic consequences. We extend their results to every dimension. We give an explicit closed-form enumeration for all $n$, $d$, and alphabet sizes $\sigma$, in which the two-dimensional coefficients $1$, $p+1$, and $p$ become $r_d(p,v)=p^{\binom{v}{2}}\binom{d}{v}_p$, with $\binom{d}{v}_p$ the Gaussian binomial; it extends to configurations with a prescribed number of active cells and to all finite abelian groups. The case of prime $n$ recovers, in complement form, a result of Castillo-Ramirez and Gadouleau; the multi-prime closed form and the dynamical consequences beyond the stabilizer inclusion are new. We prove a lower bound attained exactly when $n$ is prime, and upper bounds, among them $(2^d-1+2\log_2 n)\,\sigma^{n^d/2}$. As $d$ grows, the symmetry probability decays as $\sigma^{-c\,n^d}$ with $c\to1-1/p_1(n)$, set solely by the smallest prime factor of $n$, and the symmetry advantage of the side $p+1$ over a prime side $p$ inverts within an explicit window around $d_c(p)\approx p\ln 2$. Under the necessary hypothesis of translation-equivariant neighborhoods, shift-symmetry is irreversible, the per-prime symmetry ranks never decrease, and non-symmetric tasks are unsolvable from symmetric inputs. We give a detection algorithm with worst-case cost $O(n^d\sum_{p\mid n}\frac{p^d-1}{p-1})$ and an average-case analysis, exact for each subgroup test. The mathematical content of every numbered statement is formally verified in Lean 4, and the correspondence between each theorem, lemma, proposition, and corollary and its formal statement was audited by hand.
item.dc:creator: Peter Banda, John Caughman, Tobi Lehman

item.title: Postcritically Finite Unicritical Polynomials over CM Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.16354v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A rational map of degree at least two is postcritically finite (PCF) if every critical point has a finite forward orbit. For the unicritical family $f_{d,c}(z)=z^d+c$ with $d\ge2$, we call $c$ a PCF parameter if $f_{d,c}$ is PCF. As discussed by Baker and DeMarco, these parameters are analogous to $j$-invariants of elliptic curves with complex multiplication. For every $d\ge2$, we determine which PCF parameters lie in a CM field. The same list gives all PCF parameters over the maximal abelian extension of $\mathbb{Q}$. This extends the classifications of Noytaptim and Petsche over the maximal totally real extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ and of Ferraguti and Pagano over quadratic number fields. The proof uses the totally real classification in degree two, orbit bounds, Kronecker's theorem, Goksel's unit theorem, Lam--Leung's short-sum classification, cyclotomic averages, and known irreducibility results.
item.dc:creator: Kaoru Sano

item.title: Topological Entropy of Group Cellular Automata is Effectively Computable
item.description: arXiv:2611.16746v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Topological entropy is a fundamental invariant of dynamical systems, quantifying their complexity. For cellular automata, however, determining topological entropy is generally algorithmically intractable. We study group cellular automata, namely cellular automata over a finite group alphabet whose global map is a group endomorphism. In dimension one, we decompose topological entropy into two one-sided components describing information propagating from the left and from the right in space--time. We introduce finite families of left and right traces and prove that the entropy is the sum of their growth rates. Hence, the entropy is completely determined by the growth rate of a fixed-width family of space--time patterns. This reduction from arbitrarily large windows to uniformly bounded width yields an effective procedure for computing the entropy. In particular, the entropy of every one-dimensional group cellular automaton is the logarithm of a positive integer. Using Pontryagin duality and the Bridge Theorem between topological and algebraic entropy, we also derive an explicit formula for linear cellular automata over $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^n$ in terms of their characteristic polynomial. Moreover, in every dimension $D\geq 2$, a group cellular automaton is either equicontinuous with zero entropy or sensitive to initial conditions with infinite entropy. Combined with decidability of equicontinuity, this implies that topological entropy is effectively computable from the local rule in every dimension. Thus, group cellular automata form a natural nontrivial class in which algebraic structure restores computability of topological entropy.
item.dc:creator: Niccol\`o Castronuovo, Alberto Dennunzio, Jarkko Kari, Luciano Margara

item.title: Averaging Principle and Uniform Large Deviations for Time-Dependent Slow-Fast Systems via Young-Rough Integration
item.description: arXiv:2611.16762v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The main aim of this work is to investigate the limiting behavior and asymptotic properties of time-dependent slow-fast stochastic dynamical systems. The slow component is driven by a stochastic process with H\"older-continuous paths of regularity greater than 1/2, while the fast component is driven by a Brownian rough path. We introduce a novel Young-rough integration framework tailored to such systems and establish well-posedness results, providing the analytical foundation for further asymptotic analysis. Building on this framework, we employ Khasminskii's time-discretization method to establish the strong convergence of the slow component to the solution of the corresponding averaged equation in the L^p-sense. Furthermore, when the driving noise in the slow equation is specified as a fractional Brownian motion, we apply the weak convergence approach to establish a uniform large deviation principle for the slow component, uniformly over compact sets of initial conditions, in the H\"older topology.
item.dc:creator: Wenting Xu

item.title: Composition loci, invariant Bezoutians, and finite-orbit correspondences
item.description: arXiv:2611.16763v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute projective degrees of composition loci for polynomial and rational maps of the projective line. For normalized polynomials of degree $rs$ with a right composition factor of degree $s$, a projective-bundle construction gives the degree $S(r+s-2,r)$. We extend this calculation to composition chains, and obtain $S(r+s-1,r)$ in the uncentered normalization used for decomposable interpolation. For rational maps, a Grassmann-bundle model gives a Pl\"ucker degree formula and an interpretation by prescribed critical points. We relate these loci to factorization of the Bezoutian in the ring of symmetric polynomials, where factors correspond to monodromy orbits on unordered pairs. Fried's polynomial criterion then determines the invariant reducibility locus. For rational maps we determine its composition components when a marked pole fiber has exactly one ramified point and at least one unramified point. The qualitative equivalence between finite full orbits and a first integral is already known. We give a direct proof from forward stabilization, with an explicit test using bounded forward orbits and with quotient fibers identified at every point. We also determine when absolute and invariant irreducibility differ and give a growth formula for a class of translation correspondences.
item.dc:creator: Ragni Piene, Boris Shapiro

item.title: Intrinsic reduction data and the loci related to indeterminacy of iterate maps for rational functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.16784v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of not necessarily characteristic $0$, and $d,n$ be integers $\ge 2$. We first formulate the dynamical moduli spaces of rational functions defined over $k$ in terms of the intrinsic reduction data of non-archimedean rational functions. As an application, we show that the locus $C_{d,n}$ of semistable intrinsic reduction data in degree $d$ whose $n$th iteration is defined and unstable is of codimension $d$ in the intrinsic reduction data space of degree $d$, settling a conjecture of Kiwi and Nie, and show that the image of $C_{d,n}$ in the compactified dynamical moduli $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{d,k}$ is of dimension $\le d-2$ and the equality holds precisely either if $d$ is even or if $d\ge 5$ is odd and $(4/d)^n<1/(d-3)$ and determine the dimensions even for all the five exceptional pairs $(d,n)$, in addition describing the images of $C_{3,n}$ themselves. We also determine the indeterminacy of iterate maps either on the intrinsic reduction data spaces or on the compactified dynamical moduli spaces.
item.dc:creator: Y\^usuke Okuyama

item.title: Stochastic Kernel Mode Decomposition: Information, Uncertainty, and Conditional Regime Inference
item.description: arXiv:2611.16874v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When do mode energies preserve regime information as measurement quality changes? Stochastic Kernel Mode Decomposition (sKMD) fits joint regime laws on signed KMD mode coordinates and transfers the reference mode posterior to regime probabilities and conditional reconstructions. For centered Gaussian regimes with independently varying known noise variances, fixed coordinate energies retain the full regime posterior precisely when all classes share their cross-covariances and class variances can differ only at isolated vertices of the covariance graph. We extend the characterization to nonzero means and show that freely varying correlated noise forces a fixed linear log-odds decoder to retain the full quadratic feature span even for two distinct centered regimes. At fixed quality, a three-regime example has no sufficient two-energy basis. Its smallest Bayes log-loss gap over bases of condition number at most $\kappa$ has sharp order $\kappa^{-1}$. Exact Bayes energy posteriors supply numerical gap estimates for specified bases. Additional bounds relate feature compression, independently learned mode spans and sensor-noise error to log loss. Two controlled experiments with 64 independent panels each show that signed information can improve prediction over energy summaries, while integration gives small gains over strong signed controls and depends on how the competing point rule is calibrated and how accurately observation noise is measured.
item.dc:creator: Boumediene Hamzi, Houman Owhadi

item.title: Kac lemma on noncommutative probability spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.16972v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove non-commutative Kac's formula for actions of countable groups. We replace the return time functions by suitable projections in von Neumann algebras. Moreover, we prove a generalised Kac's formula in the non-commutative setting which extends the allocation construction of Meyerovitch and Weiss and is motivated by the random Kac inequality of Aaronson.
item.dc:creator: Tattwamasi Amrutam, Diptesh Saha, Xumin Wang

item.title: Irreversible dynamics for ideal fluids on Riemannian manifolds: metriplectic energy-conserving alternatives to Navier-Stokes
item.description: arXiv:2611.17049v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For modelling dissipative phenomena such as friction, diffusion and viscosity, the Hamiltonian framework has a key limitation: once the Casimir invariants are fixed, Hamiltonian flows preserve phase-space volume, which rules out relaxation to equilibrium. Thus modelling dissipation requires modifying the Hamiltonian structure. Following the metriplectic (equivalently, GENERIC) approach, we add to the Hamiltonian vector field a dissipative term generated by a symmetric bracket, here constructed from a Riemannian metric. The resulting flow conserves the energy, and optionally further invariants, while driving a chosen generalised entropy monotonically, which makes the dynamics irreversible; when the entropy is bounded on energy level sets in the direction in which it is driven, it acts as a Lyapunov functional. We apply this construction to ideal fluids on compact Riemannian manifolds, choosing Casimirs of the Lie-Poisson bracket as entropies. In two dimensions, dissipating enstrophy yields the already-known energy-constrained Navier-Stokes equations, which include a nonlocal term restoring energy balance. In three dimensions, where enstrophy is no longer a Casimir, we derive new irreversible models. For incompressible and compressible fluids carrying an advected scalar, dissipating potential enstrophy or higher potential-vorticity moments gives a nonlinear, anisotropic diffusion that acts to align the gradients of the scalar and of the potential vorticity. For a purely incompressible fluid, taking helicity as the entropy gives a first-order, non-smoothing dissipative term whose stationary states are Beltrami fields.
item.dc:creator: Erwin Luesink, Archishman Saha, Tanya Schmah, Cristina Stoica

item.title: Analysis of non-linear fractal functions on PCF self-similar sets
item.description: arXiv:2505.10455v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article addresses three problems: (1) the construction of a general nonlinear fractal interpolation function on post-critically finite (PCF) self-similar sets; (2) the study of the energy and normal derivatives of uniform nonlinear fractal functions; and (3) the estimation of the box-counting dimensions of the proposed fractal functions on the Sierpi\'nski gasket and the von Koch curve. We present a general framework for constructing attractors and fractal functions on PCF self-similar sets using Edelstein contractions. Further, we derive upper and lower bounds for the box-counting dimensions of the graphs of nonlinear interpolants. Finally, we provide several graphical and numerical examples to illustrate the construction and estimate the dimensions for different data sets.
item.dc:creator: Aaryan Dharmesh Shah, Sangita Jha, Anarul Islam Mondal

item.title: Ulam Approximation for Nonautonomous Systems: Equivariant Measures and Linear Response
item.description: arXiv:2606.02889v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Despite the prevalence of nonautonomous systems in applications, their statistical properties are much less understood than in the autonomous setting. Building on recent results on response theory for nonautonomous systems, we study the approximation of equivariant families and of their linear response by Ulam-type finite-dimensional reductions. First, we show that coarse-graining procedures associated with the classical Ulam method, and more generally with suitable finite-element projections, such as those often associated with the Koopman/Kolmogorov operator-informed analysis of dynamical systems, provide rigorous approximation of equivariant families for sequential systems with memory loss. Second, for systems whose transfer operators are regularising, we prove that the linear response of the reduced finite-state Markov model converges to the projected linear response of the original system. We illustrate the results with numerical experiments on simple but representative time-dependent diffusive models. These results provide a rigorous foundation for the use of Markov approximations in the study of statistical properties of nonautonomous complex systems which almost invariably relies on finite-scale and finite-precision descriptions of their states and dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Galatolo, Valerio Lucarini, Isaia Nisoli

item.title: Zero-Threshold Discrepancies for Multiple Correlation Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2606.25581v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the zero-threshold lifting problem for polynomial multiple correlation sequences with respect to the measure-theoretic pro-nilfactor. The structure theory for polynomial multiple averages implies that, at every positive threshold, positivity on the pro-nilfactor lifts to positivity in the original system, except on a set of zero upper Banach density. We demonstrate that this lifting property does not hold at the zero threshold. Specifically, we construct an ergodic system and two sets of positive measure for which the pro-nilfactor correlation is positive along a set of times with positive upper density, while the corresponding exact correlation vanishes on this set. This provides a negative answer to a question posed by Glasscock, Koutsogiannis, Le, Moreira, Richter, and Robertson. %\cite{GKLMMRR}. Additionally, we prove a corresponding rigidity property. For any ergodic system, any essentially distinct family of integer polynomials vanishing at the origin, and any tuple of non-negative bounded functions, the zero-threshold discrepancy set is not piecewise syndetic.
item.dc:creator: Kangbo Ouyang, Jiahao Qiu, Xiangdong Ye

item.title: Lie Meets Network Dynamics: Exact Macroscopic Reductions (Finite Systems)
item.description: arXiv:2607.12210v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a unified theory for exact dimensional reductions in network dynamical systems using Lie-Scheffers theory. For network dynamical systems with mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure, we prove that networks of $n$ nodes with local dimension $d$ can be exactly reduced from $nd$ dimensions to a fixed macroscopic system of dimension $md$, where $m$ is the number of fundamental solutions required by the nodal dynamics. Crucially, the superposition rule resulting from the Lie-algebraic structure allows the mean-field coupling to be expressed explicitly in terms of the macroscopic variables, yielding a closed self-consistent system independent of the network size $n$. This reduction collapses the high-dimensional network flow onto (typically) low dimensional invariant manifolds parameterized by $\gamma=d(n-m)$ independent constants of motion. We illustrate the theory on systems with mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure: ensembles of Riccati equations (recovering known reductions for the Kuramoto model and Theta neuron model), recently studied quasi-linear ODEs, as well as a new class of generalized Bernoulli equations; we explicitly derive the macroscopic flows and conserved quantities for each case. Thus, our theory rigorously explains known reductions and provides a systematic method to discover new ones.
item.dc:creator: Erik Andreas Martens, Sanjay Dharmavaram

item.title: Bifurcation of periodic and antiperiodic solutions in non-autonomous potential-type delay systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.14538v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As a continuation of our previous work, where bifurcations of periodic and antiperiodic orbits near an equilibrium were studied for autonomous differential delay systems with one or two delays, this paper investigates bifurcations of periodic and antiperiodic solutions for five classes of non-autonomous potential delay differential systems with multiple delays. By reformulating these systems as generalized Hamiltonian systems on Euclidean spaces, we apply the Hamiltonian bifurcation theory recently developed by the author to establish alternative bifurcation results of both Fadell-Rabinowitz and Rabinowitz type.
item.dc:creator: Guangcun Lu

item.title: Orbit equivalence and total weak mixing of free group actions
item.description: arXiv:2608.20165v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the orbit equivalence class of every free ergodic probability-measure-preserving (pmp) action of a free group contains a totally weak mixing action. Equivalently, every ergodic treeable pmp equivalence relation of cost $n\in\mathbf{N}\cup\{\infty\}$ is generated by a free totally weak mixing action of $\mathbf{F}_n$. This answers a question of Miller and Tserunyan. The proof goes by considering a Polish space of edge slidings along a fixed mixing transformation and proving that for every $w\not=e\in\mathbf{F}_n$ the set of edge slidings that produce an action with $w$ weakly mixing forms a comeager set.
item.dc:creator: Konrad Wr\'{o}bel

item.title: On the topological dynamical system of tilings
item.description: arXiv:2609.06310v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Tilings can be studied from the perspective of dynamical systems and ergodic theory. Some fundamental features of tiling spaces as topological dynamical systems, such as the continuity of the action by translation, the compactness with the tiling metric, and the minimality of the system generated by a repetitive tiling, are among the most frequently mentioned basic facts in the dynamical theory of aperiodic order. Nonetheless, despite their classical status, complete proofs of these facts, together with the preliminary material they rely on, to the best of our knowledge, are not available in the literature. The purpose of this survey is to give a self-contained, rigorous, and pedagogical treatment of these foundations with detailed preliminary material. We hope that this exposition will provide a useful reference and contribute to a clearer and more accessible understanding of the fundamentals of the theory of tiling dynamical systems.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Pablo Santander

item.title: On normal forms and first integrals of planar maps at elliptic fixed points
item.description: arXiv:2609.21417v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study real-analytic planar maps, that admit a real-analytic first integral with a non-degenerate extremum, in a neighbourhood of an elliptic fixed point. We prove that, if the map preserves an analytic area form, it is real-analytically and symplectically conjugate to a twist map, both in the resonant and in the non-resonant case. Using an example, we show that without the area-preservation assumption the conclusion fails. We then prove that a second, continuous, first integral is either a function of the first one or forces the map to be periodic, in which case the map is analytically (and, when area-preserving, symplectically) conjugate to its linear part. We illustrate our results, we study the McMillan map, and a planar map obtained from the Adler--Yamilov Yang--Baxter map.
item.dc:creator: Stavros Anastassiou

item.title: Existence and Uniqueness Proof for the Transport Equation and the Orthogonal Dynamics Equation for Zwanzig's Projection on Gaussian Spaces: A Vanishing Viscosity Method
item.description: arXiv:2610.18647v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the existence of unique solutions ${u\in H^1(0,T;L^2_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n))\cap L^2(0,T;H^1_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n))}$ of the transport equation $u_t=F\cdot\nabla u+f$ and the orthogonal dynamics equation ${u_t= Q_\text{Z} (F\cdot\nabla) Q_\text{Z} u+f}$, where $F$ is a time-independent vector field, $f$ is a forcing term, $P_\text{Z}=1-Q_\text{Z}$ is a Zwanzig projection (conditional expectation) on $L^2_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n)$ defined by $P_\text{Z}h \propto \int h(\cdot ,y) \rho(\cdot,y)\rm{d}y$, and $\gamma$ is the standard Gaussian measure with density $\rho$. To this end, we develop a vanishing viscosity method based on the maximal regularity theory for the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operator on $L^2_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n)$. The following assumptions guarantee the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions: ${f\in H^1(0,T;L^2_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n))\cap L^2(0,T;H^1_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n))}$, ${g\in H^1_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n)}$, $F\in W^{1,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $\rm{ess\,sup}_{\mathbb{R}^n}\left(x\cdot F-\rm{div}F\right) < \infty$, where $g$ denotes the initial value function.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Widder

item.title: A five-species counterexample to the Hofbauer--Kon--Saito conjecture on qualitative permanence
item.description: arXiv:2610.38374v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hofbauer, Kon and Saito showed that a Lotka-Volterra interaction matrix $A$ with negative diagonal can be qualitatively permanent only if (C1) every cycle of length $\ge 2$ of $A$ is nonpositive and (C2) every negative cycle contains exactly one negative entry. They conjectured that these conditions are also sufficient, and proved this for $n\le 3$. We give a $5\times 5$ integer matrix with seven nonzero off-diagonal entries that satisfies (C1) and (C2) but is not qualitatively permanent. For an explicit integer growth vector, in which one species is an obligate consumer as the definition allows, the system has an interior equilibrium, and an asymptotically stable heteroclinic cycle on the boundary of the orthant attracts an open set of interior orbits. Adding non-interacting species gives counterexamples for every $n\ge 5$. The interactions form a one-way feedback loop together with a predator of two prey. The verification is elementary except for one heteroclinic connection, which lies in a face that is not Volterra-Lyapunov stable. For it we prove a connection lemma based on invasion graphs, which reduces the question to a smaller, stable face. The failure is robust. It persists under small perturbations, including weak additional interactions, so every sign pattern that satisfies (C1) and (C2) and contains ours is a counterexample, and it occurs for an open cone of growth vectors. For $n\ge 6$ there are also counterexamples in which every species grows when alone. Finally, we announce that the conjecture holds for $n=4$ and that, for $n=5$, four minimal sign patterns characterise its failure.
item.dc:creator: Miruna-Mihaela Beldiman, Andrei-Dan Halanay

item.title: Nonequilibrium Transient Centers in Continuous-Time Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.41930v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Analysis of mathematical models in ecology and epidemiology often emphasizes asymptotic dynamics, such as stable equilibria, periodic orbits, and attractors. However, many biologically relevant trajectories exhibit long transient dynamics in which a relevant observable evolves slowly for an extended period before a comparatively rapid transition occurs. On finite time scales relevant to data collection, management, and intervention, such transient behavior can be more informative than the eventual asymptotic outcome. In this work, we study long-lasting and slowly varying transient dynamics in continuous-time systems through the framework of nonequilibrium transient centers. These centers are points in the state space near which the observable can remain nearly constant for a long time, even when the full state is not near an equilibrium. We develop finite-time escape criteria for identifying such centers and their reachable counterparts. These criteria provide practical conditions under which nearby trajectories can remain in a slow regime for a long period of time before eventually leaving it. We apply the theory to an epidemic model with delay of stability loss. In this model, trajectories may remain close to the disease-free manifold for a long time before the infectious population resurges. The framework developed here describes this behavior as slow evolution near a nonequilibrium transient center followed by finite-time escape from the slow regime.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Pasion, Felicia Magpantay

item.title: Round-Based Contagion Generates Chaos from Oscillatory Dynamics: A Two-Stage Contagion Map
item.description: arXiv:2611.08353v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many social processes unfold in rounds, such as elections, meetings or turns of a game, in which individuals update synchronously. We show that this round structure can turn a regular oscillation into chaos. In Katriel's differential equations, two-stage contagion (adoption after two contacts with adopters) combined with population turnover produces bistability and relaxation oscillations, but no chaos. From the elementary reactions we derive a deterministic map $F_\tau$ for a large population updated in rounds of length $\tau$: each individual makes at most one transition per round, events compete as exponential risks, and adoptions take effect from the next round. Katriel's equations are recovered as $\tau\to0$. For short rounds the map follows the relaxation cycle, and the phase of successive outbreaks obeys a circle homeomorphism, which excludes chaos. As the rounds lengthen, this circle map loses invertibility and the invariant curve breaks down; once a round lasts about two mean adoption times, comparable to the duration of an outbreak, the attractor is chaotic, while Katriel's equations remain on a periodic relaxation cycle. With the probability $p$ of adoption after a single contact as bifurcation parameter, the map goes from extinction through a window of chaos to a stable equilibrium; for $\beta/\gamma=46$, $\mu/\gamma=0.002$, $\gamma\tau=5.5$ the window is $0.023\le p\le0.056$, bounded by the invasion threshold and by a boundary crisis, whereas Katriel's equations oscillate for $0.022<p<0.41$. Chaos is supported by the Lyapunov spectrum (Kaplan--Yorke dimension $1.81$), the correlation dimension, the 0-1 test, ordinal-pattern complexity, saddle periodic orbits and a horseshoe of the phase map. One-stage contagion, $p=0$ and permanent adoption showed no chaos.
